section.sectionSummaryBrief: By placing them before the ark as emissaries of the congregation, Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi] caused all of Israel to be drawn after that congregation and after the emissaries, thereby removing the barriers.
section.t: And one can explain the elucidation of this,
that by Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi] placing them before the ark and making them the emissaries of the congregation of all Israel,
he effected this upon all of Israel
(even upon those who knew nothing at all of the entire matter)52
that they would be drawn after the congregation that was present at the time of the prayer of Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa and his sons,
and all the more so after Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa and his sons themselves
(the emissaries of the congregation),
and therefore,
the arousal of the congregation that was present at the time of the prayer,
and their prayer of Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa and his sons,
effected in the innermost aspect upon all of Israel,
and through this the barriers were nullified.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: Prayer alone brings a change in the world from a transcendent light, but when prayer includes Torah, the light itself is drawn down and felt in the change.
section.t: And behold, that which was explained above
(section 4)
that the drawing down of the light that is above the chain of descent, which comes through prayer, is that through it a change is effected in the matters of the world
(and not that the light itself is drawn downward),
this is regarding prayer as it is in its own right.
But when the prayer is in a manner that also includes the aspect of Torah,
one can say,
that in the drawing down that comes through this prayer,
there are both virtues.
That the root of the drawing down is above and beyond, to no end,
and that the light itself is drawn downward.
That is,
that in the change that is effected in the world
(that the sick person is healed and the like)
there is felt in revelation not only the change in the world
(the result of the drawing down)
but also the Divine light through which the change is effected.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: When prayer includes the request "Ad-noy, open my lips," which draws God's own prayer, it combines the virtue of prayer (arousal from below) and Torah (drawing from above), so the change in the world reveals the Divine light.
section.t: And one can connect this with what was explained above
(section 3)

that the request "Ad-noy, open my lips, and my mouth will declare Your praise" at the beginning of the Silent Prayer is that a person's prayer should be in a manner that through it "Your praise" is drawn,
the prayer of the Holy One, blessed be He,
for when the prayer is in this manner, there are in it both virtues.
The virtue of prayer—the work from below
[that reaches above and beyond, to no end,
"You yearn for the work of Your hands"],
and the virtue of Torah—a drawing down from above.
And through the union of the two aspects in the work of prayer,
that even the request of the human is in the manner of "my mouth will declare Your praise,"
through this,
even in the drawing down that comes through prayer there are
(analogous to)
the two aspects.
That through it a change is effected in the lower realm,
and that the change in the lower realm is in a manner that the Divine light through which the change is effected is felt in it.
